summary: Adds three endpoints: a user search by name, a per-key request counter guarded by a mutex, and an upstream status probe. main.go registers all three.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: Search puts the name query parameter straight into the SQL text with Sprintf. Nothing escapes or binds the value.
findings.consequence: Any caller of GET /users can inject SQL. An injected query can read or change any data the database user can reach.
findings.fix: Pass name to QueryContext as a bound parameter. Remove the Sprintf call.
findings.suggested_change: rows, err := h.DB.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)

findings.title: Mutex left locked on missing key
findings.problem: Count locks h.mu before it checks the key. The empty-key branch then returns without unlocking h.mu.
findings.consequence: One request to GET /count without a key leaves h.mu locked for good. Every later Count request then blocks forever.
findings.fix: Check the key before taking the lock. Alternatively, defer the unlock right after Lock.

findings.title: Response body closed before error check
findings.problem: fetchStatus defers resp.Body.Close before it checks err. When http.Get fails, resp is nil.
findings.consequence: An unreachable upstream makes Upstream panic on a nil pointer. The client gets a dropped connection instead of the intended 502.
findings.fix: Move the deferred Close below the error check.

findings.title: New handlers have no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds Search, Count and Upstream, but the repository has no test files. No test exercises any of the new handlers.
findings.consequence: No test catches regressions in the new handlers. That includes the lock and nil pointer bugs in this change.
findings.fix: Add httptest-based tests for each handler. Cover the empty-key and upstream-failure paths.

dropped.reason: This hit flags the same Sprintf query that the c1 finding already raises.
